keyVerseText: In the seventh year of Jehu Jehoash began to reign; and forty years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
rootMeaning: The root of צִבְיָּה (Tsibyâh) comes from צְבִיָּה (tsᵉbîyâh), meaning 'roe' or 'female gazelle.' This literal sense of a graceful and swift animal adds a layer of poetic imagery to the name, suggesting qualities such as beauty, agility, and perhaps gentleness or innocence. Thus, the name Tsibyâh carries not only a personal identity but also evokes the natural elegance associated with the gazelle.
usageInScripture: The word צִבְיָּה appears twice in Scripture, consistently as a proper name referring to a woman—specifically, the mother of King Joash of Judah. Translations render the name as 'Zibiah,' maintaining the connection to the original Hebrew. This consistency in usage highlights the name's function as a personal identifier linked to a notable figure in the Davidic royal lineage, emphasizing her origin from Beersheba.
theologicalSignificance: The name Tsibyâh, rooted in the imagery of a gazelle, enriches our understanding of biblical characters by linking them to the natural world God created, reflecting His attention to detail even in names. As the mother of King Joash, Tsibyâh represents a vital link in the covenantal history of Judah, showing how God works through individuals of grace and dignity to fulfill His promises. Her inclusion in Scripture by name affirms the value of godly lineage and the providential role of women in salvation history. Recognizing the meaning behind her name invites believers to appreciate the beauty and purpose God weaves into every life within His redemptive plan.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Kings 12:1 states, 'In the seventh year of Jehu Jehoash began to reign; and forty years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.' The mention of Tsibyâh here grounds the king's identity in his maternal heritage, highlighting the importance of lineage and origin. Her name, evoking the gazelle, subtly suggests qualities that may have influenced or characterized the king's reign. This detail enriches the historical narrative by connecting the royal line to a woman of noted background and grace.
